project_name: Vermaland La Osa Data Center Campus
status_detail: Rezoning/planning-stage megasite south of Eloy; initial public materials described up to 3GW/59 data centers, later reporting says the proposal was scaled back to 11 data-center buildings after local opposition.
notes: Capacity reflects maximum early proposal; current scaled-back capacity may be lower and should be updated from Pinal County final entitlement records.

status_detail: Tract announced acquisition of 2,069 acres in Buckeye for a master-planned data center park with up to 20 million sq ft across as many as 40 data centers; working with utility on up to 1.8GW.
notes: Arizona Corporation Commission described a 2,000-acre Buckeye data center park with $20B investment plans; source naming varies between Tract Buckeye and Tract Phoenix.

status_detail: Arizona Land Consulting acquired about 2,000 acres west of Phoenix and is pursuing entitlements for a potential 1.5GW data center; development timeline not available.
notes: Backed by Chamath Palihapitiya/Social Capital per DCD; early design/entitlement stage.

status_detail: Ryan Companies filed to pivot a planned industrial/warehouse site at Estrella and Houser roads into a 400MW data center campus; Eloy Planning and Zoning Commission recommended rezoning approval in January 2025.
notes: Public descriptions vary between three buildings/855k sf and larger 1.25M-1.4M sf concepts; retained at project level.

status_detail: Novva announced a 160-acre southeast Mesa campus along Ellsworth/Warner roads with five data halls, 1.3M sq ft of data halls, and 300MW; first 96MW phase targeted for late 2026.
notes: Official Novva pages confirm 300MW campus; early public codename was Project Borealis.

status_detail: Menlo Digital describes a 38-acre five-building hyperscale campus at 4801 E Thistle Landing Dr with a dedicated onsite substation supporting more than 257MW utility power and 180MW critical IT load; local reporting notes city easement actions and neighborhood opposition.
notes: Year uses reported early 2027 data hall delivery; Cleanview lists expected 2026, but Menlo-linked material points to substation service by Dec. 2026 and deliveries in early 2027.

status_detail: Prime broke ground in May 2026 on the first three buildings of a five-building PHX01 campus in Avondale; planned full build is 240MW critical IT load across 1.3M sq ft on 66.5 acres.
notes: First three 48MW buildings reportedly secured by a leading hyperscaler; remaining two available for additional demand.

project_name: NTT Global Data Centers Phoenix Mesa Campus
status_detail: NTT's 102-acre Elliot Road Technology Corridor campus was announced as 240MW and 1.5M sq ft; 2026 reporting says plans were revised to combine buildings six and seven, reducing the campus from seven to six buildings.
notes: First 36MW PH1 building was targeted for early 2022; status marked construction because later filings show continuing campus revisions.

status_detail: EdgeCore's official Phoenix/Mesa campus page lists 496MW of critical IT load, 2.7M sq ft, five data centers, and an 84-acre campus built for cloud and AI workloads.
notes: Campus includes operational and likely phased capacity; project retained as a single campus.

status_detail: Meta/Redale acquired about 396 acres at Elliot and Ellsworth; campus expanded to five buildings totaling more than 2.5M sq ft, with completion previously targeted for 2026.
notes: Capacity not consistently public; cost reported above $1B after expansion.

status_detail: Amazon filed pre-submittal documents for a Mesa site off Elliot Road, with two approximately 227,000 sq ft data center buildings on a 42.9-acre parcel acquired in December 2021.
notes: One of two separate AWS Mesa land positions; keep separate from Pecos Road campus.

project_name: Amazon AWS Mesa Pecos Road Campus
status_detail: Amazon filed for a second Mesa data center site at/near 10464 E Pecos Road, with two approximately 227,000 sq ft data center buildings on a 71.3-acre parcel.
notes: Some articles describe 'four data centers' because the two Mesa campuses each contain two main buildings.

status_detail: Google started work on a roughly $1B data center campus on more than 185 acres near Elliot and Sossaman roads; Mesa materials later reviewed Phase II/Redhawk HUB plans.
notes: Development agreement required first phase by July 2025 and $600M capex; public MW not found in accessible sources.

status_detail: QTS filed plans for a 375-acre Phoenix 3 campus north of Camelback Road and west of Loop 303, with 16 buildings totaling around 3M sq ft and 750MW of critical capacity; QTS website lists PHX 3 building addresses on W Camelback Road.
notes: Jurisdiction/location is reported as Glendale area by some sources and Litchfield Park addresses by QTS.

status_detail: Mesa Planning and Zoning Commission approved/recommended the CyrusOne campus at Elliot and Ellsworth roads: up to five two-story buildings of about 286,530 sq ft each, totaling around 1.4M sq ft on 62 acres.
notes: Capacity not public in accessible reports; separate from CyrusOne's existing Chandler campus.

aliases: Legacy Park east data center campus
status_detail: Pacific Proving proposed a 178-acre Mesa campus north of Pecos Road and east of Ellsworth Road with six data centers, 32 data halls, about 1.4M sq ft, and 360MW; Mesa planning commission recommended approval and sent it to City Council.
notes: Early entitlement-stage project on former GM proving grounds land.

status_detail: Microsoft operates an El Mirage data center campus at 12901 W Olive Avenue; PHX80 is operational, PHX81 and PHX82 permitted/under construction, and PHX83 was filed as a 245,500 sq ft fifth building expansion.
notes: Microsoft's West US 3 region launched in June 2021; accessible sources do not give campus MW.

status_detail: Microsoft says it operates datacenters in Goodyear as part of the Greater Phoenix/West US 3 footprint; DCD reports Microsoft owns more than 450 acres along MC-85/Lower Buckeye Road and Citrus/Indian School roads with two Goodyear data centers.
notes: Separated from El Mirage because Microsoft identifies both cities as operating datacenter locations.

status_detail: Compass lists a 212MW campus in Goodyear; earlier Goodyear/Compass announcements described an eight-building campus capable of up to 350MW with an onsite 230kV substation.
notes: Capacity_mw uses current Compass market page; older master plan described possible 350MW buildout.

status_detail: Compass market page states it is developing a 108MW campus in El Mirage; DCD also notes Compass is developing a campus in El Mirage near Microsoft's footprint.
notes: Limited public detail beyond Compass market listing; retained due explicit developer source.

status_detail: Stream's 157-acre Goodyear hyperscale campus supports up to 280MW critical load across more than 2M sq ft; first two of seven buildings are actively serving tenants, with five remaining buildings in development.
notes: Official page also notes dedicated APS substation with ultimate power capacity of 480MW.

status_detail: STACK lists PHX01 in Avondale with 225MW critical capacity for cloud and AI deployments; tracker sources describe planned phases through 2029 at Avondale Techplex.
notes: Some trackers split PHX01 into PHX01A/B/C; this JSONL keeps it as one campus-level project.

status_detail: STACK lists PHX02 in Central Phoenix with 250MW capacity and a dedicated onsite substation; earlier Data Center Frontier reporting described a major Phoenix campus plan.
notes: Current operating/under-construction status not fully clear from accessible official page; marked planned conservatively.

status_detail: Aligned's Union Hills Phoenix campus at 2500 W Union Hills Drive opened in 2017 and expanded in 2018; current reporting describes three buildings totaling 550,000 sq ft and 180MW.
notes: Separate from Aligned's newer Glendale campus.

status_detail: Aligned broke ground on PHX-13, a 72MW building, at a 100-acre Glendale campus planned for roughly 1M sq ft and 252MW critical power across four facilities.
notes: Capacity_mw reflects reported campus critical power; first building PHX-13 is 72MW.

status_detail: Iron Mountain's Phoenix campus includes AZP-1 and AZP-2 with 89MW total capacity and a third Phoenix data center AZP-3 in development; AZP-3 is described as a 36MW project.
notes: Capacity_mw sums AZP-1/AZP-2 official 89MW plus reported/planned AZP-3 36MW.

status_detail: EdgeConneX is developing a Mesa campus on land near Loop 202 and Elliot Road; public reporting describes 50 to 93 acres available/planned for build-to-suit data center development and an EdgeConneX blog says 168MVA phased through 2027.
notes: MW is treated as MVA-equivalent from EdgeConneX public blog; construction contractor page confirms a 400,000 sf Mesa facility underway.

status_detail: Vantage's Phoenix campus is located at 45 S Bullard Avenue in Goodyear; Vantage/Goodyear announcements describe a 160MW campus across three facilities, while later design material references four AZ1 facilities totaling 160MW and additional phases.
notes: Corgan notes AZ14 became operational in 2025 and references AZ15; capacity retained at 160MW from official/city sources.

status_detail: Edged opened its PHX01-1 facility in April 2026 at 8811 E Warner Road in Mesa; the two-story 210,000 sq ft facility delivers 36MW and uses waterless cooling.
notes: Official Edged announcement confirms 36MW critical capacity.

status_detail: 5C Data Centers announced a new Phoenix region with PHX01, a 140,000 sq ft AI-focused facility a few miles west of downtown Phoenix at/near 2802 W Palm Lane, planned for 20MW critical IT power and go-live in 2025; later trackers list it under construction.
notes: Go-live may have slipped from the original 2025 announcement; status marked construction based on current tracker.

status_detail: Comarch's North American data center at 3223 S Ellsworth Road is a 32,000 to 32,400 sq ft facility; contractor source says it is 1.5MW and was completed in June 2023.
notes: Comarch originally targeted mid-2022 operations; Weitz reports June 2023 completion.

status_detail: CyrusOne's Chandler PHX1-PHX8 campus comprises eight data centers; DCD reports around 2.1M sq ft and 81MW, while CyrusOne's official page describes eight facilities with zero-water cooling.
notes: Existing operating campus, separate from new CyrusOne Mesa proposal.

project_name: Project Blue Tucson Data Center Campus
status_detail: Tucson City Council unanimously rejected the planned Project Blue AI data center campus in August 2025; prior proposal contemplated up to 10 buildings totaling 2M sq ft and 600MW, with first building targeted for 2027.
notes: Included despite rejection because brief asks to include early announcements/unconfirmed projects; AWS involvement was reported as accidentally disclosed.

status_detail: Tracker sources list a planned Davis-Monthan AFB data center in Pima County with 500MW capacity; no accessible primary project filing was found during this pass.
notes: Low-confidence tracker-only entry retained under '宁多勿漏'; needs follow-up against federal procurement/NEPA/utility records.
